gv_epilogue_texts:
Ending narration, 7 pages, and 'THE END' (file offsets 82322-82863, SNES $02:C192-$C3AF, bank 02). The staff roll string StaffRollText (file offsets 90724-92320, SNES $02:E264-$E8A0) is noted in its own part (batch A8; answers OQ-I029-5).

=== MODEL ===
The ending actor (code_00729D in gv_front_end, meta entry $57) prints EndingPage1Text to EndingPage7Text with a scene change between the fourth and fifth page; TheEndText is printed by code_01B508 (gv_up_above_trial_room_and_lisa_turbo_actors). The story: Grass Valley at sunset, the creatures looking at the sunset, a light ray that nobody notices, and Lisa alone, who now finds the sunset beautiful and believes she can be happy as her father turned the impossible into the possible.

gv_prologue_texts:
Story narration of the intro, 14 pages (file offsets 80773-82293, SNES $02:BB85-$C175, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
The intro actor (code_0066FC in gv_front_end, meta entry $56) prints the pages one after the other in address order, each on its own BG3 position (the [CUR:o] at the start of the page; $240, $280 or $300 depending on the line count). After the last page it warps to scene $0A of area 0, the Mode 7 scene (OQ-I011-4). The story: the Freil Empire under King Magridd, the inventor Dr. Leo, the deal with the king of evil Deathtoll that empties the world, and the Master sending the player to revive it as a Soul Blazer.

=== NOTES ===
- The text is printed with the intro font: the period prints as '-' and the apostrophe as a blank (the extract shows 'Dr-Leo-'). Line breaks are [N][N][N].
- The walkthrough does not quote the story; names it shares (Magridd, Leo, Deathtoll, the Master) agree. 'Freil Empire' occurs nowhere else in the project.
gv_title_texts:
Title screen, tile block and save slot menu strings (file offsets 80679-80772, 82294-82321 and 82864-83036, SNES $02:BB27-$BB84, $02:C176-$C191 and $02:C3B0-$C45C, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
TitlePushStartText and TitleCopyrightText are printed by the title actor (code_0066FC in gv_front_end, meta entry $56): the copyright block first, then 'PUSH START' at BG3 offset $4D6 ([09] = two-row glyphs). The walkthrough says the player presses Start at the title screen to reach the file selection menu. TileBlockText draws a 4x5 block of tiles at BG3 rows 11-15, columns 14-17 from the insert list entries 4-8 ([02:n]); it is printed by code_0066C6 (gv_front_end) and what it draws is not identified (OQ-I011-9).
SaveSlotMenuText draws the file selection window (DrawSaveSlotMenu in engine_title_file_select): 'Please choose a record', the column heads Name, Lev and Area, 'No1:' to 'No4:' and 'Erase record'. The four slot lines are filled in by SaveSlotLineTemplates, an 80-byte table that is really four 20-byte STRINGS, stepped by $14: [CUR:o1][02:3][CUR:o2][06:2,0450][CUR:o3][06:1,0452] and an end byte. [02:3] is the slot name (insert entry 3, $0447), [06:2,0450] the level as BCD and [06:1,0452] a word read from the save block at +$1B90, the value the file select later loads into scene_next (OQ-I011-12). The cursor offsets are $2D4, $2E8 and $2F2 for slot 1 and each next slot adds $C0.

=== NOTES ===
- The strings use the intro font: the apostrophe prints as a blank, the period as '-'.
- SaveSlotLineTemplates is typed Binary in the extract because it is mostly control codes; it is text.
lib_010000:
Camera aim: one routine, AimCameraAtPlayer (file offsets 65536-65640, SNES $02:8000-$8068, bank 02).

The camera follows the player without smoothing: AimCameraAtPlayer converts 'where the camera should be' into the signed deltas scroll_delta_x and scroll_delta_y, and ScrollCameraByDelta (lib_map_streaming) applies them in the same frame. The whole scroll model is in the lib_map_streaming block note.
lib_0108BB:
Map patch rectangles: copy a rectangle of the map to another place, and the table that holds the five boss-room patches followed by the map sizes (ApplyMapPatchRect: file offsets 67771-68053, SNES $02:88BB-$89D5; MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes: 95492-95787, SNES $02:F504-$F62B; bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
ApplyMapPatchRect copies a rectangle of metatiles (and their tile_type_map bytes) inside the BG1 map: from the source rectangle given in the record's pixel words +4 / +6 to the destination given by +0 / +1 (metatile units), width +2, height +3; then every copied cell that is on screen is queued for VRAM (16 bytes per cell in vram_write_queue, zero terminator). It is the boss-room patch: RunBossMapPatch (engine_003005) calls it with the id 0-4 stored by five boss scripts (whether the patch closes or opens the room is OQ-I024-3).

=== TABLE ===
MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes holds two tables back to back in one 296-byte part: 5 patch records of 8 bytes (entries 00-04 of the extracted rows) and, from byte $28, 128 pairs (map_width_pages, map_height_pages) indexed by location_id x 2, read by lib_scene_change_init (OQ-I026-2: the part should be split in blocks.json).
Patch record: +0 destination x, +1 destination y (metatiles), +2 width, +3 height (metatiles), +4 word source x, +6 word source y (pixels).
lib_0109D6_part1:
Metatile writers: put one metatile into the map and, when it is on screen, queue it for VRAM (file offsets 67313-67770, SNES $02:86F1-$88BA, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Both routines (1) turn the pixel position in dp$16 / $18 into a map offset (lib_map_index_helpers.PixelToMapIndex), (2) store the metatile id in the BG1 map ($7E8000) and, for SetMetatileBg1Bg2, also in the BG2 map ($7EC000), (3) rewrite the tile_type_map byte ($7F8000) from the definition (the solid flag, bit 9, of the four tile words gives bits 0 to 3: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) and (4) when the metatile lies in the view plus 16 pixels, write four (VRAM address, tile word) entries per layer to vram_write_queue ($1C7B, 4 bytes per entry, 16 per metatile) and a zero terminator; the NMI (FlushVramWriteQueue) draws them.
The queue is overwritten from its start: callers either wait for it to be empty first (SealLair) or call right after the NMI has emptied it (the tile triggers).
Callers: SealLair (green switch $FE), CheckPlayerTileTriggers / TryOpenChest (open chest $FC) and ReleaseLairAtSwitch's own map write (it writes the map bytes directly).
lib_0109D6_part3:
Inventory store (file offsets 73977-74039, SNES $02:A0F9-$A137, bank 02).

The inventory / progress table is the byte array inventory ($1B1E): entry n (1-based) is at $1B1E + n - 1, bits 0-6 hold the value (the entry number when owned), bit 7 is the 'equipped' flag (OQ-I006-2). StoreInventoryEntry is the only writer used by the item scripts (Cop0A_GiveItemIfNotOwned) and by the chest code (TryOpenChest).
lib_0118FC_part2:
Menu row chooser (file offsets 74040-74368, SNES $02:A138-$A280, bank 02; the cursor offset table is at 74359-74368).

=== MODEL ===
A cursor of one glyph (BG3 tile $2B, drawn in the cell at the row's offset and in the cell one tilemap row above it) moves between a few rows of a menu. ChooseMenuRow serves the equipment menu: rows are $80 apart in the BG3 buffer (two text rows), Up and Down move, Y cancels (carry set) and B confirms (carry clear); the equipment menu uses it with four rows (Weapon, Armor, Magic, Item) and swaps the page on the way. ChooseMenuRowAtTable is the same loop for the file-select and erase menus of engine_title_file_select: the row offsets come from TitleMenuCursorOffsets ($C0 apart) and there is no page swap; B plays the confirm sound ($18) there and the cancel and move sounds are $07 (OQ-I009-12).
Both wait for all buttons to be up (lib_text_render.WaitFrameReadButtons, which returns the high byte of joy_pressed) before reading a press and call lib_shared_01230B.BlinkChoiceCursor while waiting (it blinks the cursor glyph; menu_blink counts the frames).

=== NOTES ===
- Input: A = row count (stored in menu_count), B (after XBA) = start row, X = BG3 byte offset of the start row's cursor cell. Output: carry clear and A = row; carry set when Y was pressed. The final cursor glyph stays drawn on the last row.
- The first 'wait until released' loop gives an edge-triggered feel: joy_pressed holds a button as long as it is down (or until the latch is cleared), so a held button would otherwise repeat.
lib_0118FC_part5:
Palette and graphics handoff of the menus (file offsets 74832-74989, SNES $02:A450-$A4ED, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
The equipment menu replaces the field's VRAM character data at word $2000 with its own graphics and the palette with its own, and puts the field back on exit. LoadItemPagePalette gives the item page its palette (colours 0-127 from ItemPagePalette). RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette DMAs the 8 KB copy of graphics_04D000 that lib_02719F keeps at $7F:C000 back to VRAM word $2000 and restores palettes 11-15 (MenuSpellPalettes, 160 bytes, to cgram_buffer + $160); the scene loader (lib_027781_part3, when $0454 is set) and common_actor_0066C6.code_0066DE call it too. LoadEquippedMagicGfx then puts the graphics and palette of the equipped spell on top.
On the menu exit the order is RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, RestoreCgramBuffer (which overwrites the whole CGRAM buffer, including the colours just written) and LoadEquippedMagicGfx: the spell palette is loaded last so it survives.

=== NOTES ===
- What graphics_04D000 is (field BG or shared tile set): OQ-I009-13.
- Spell n = equipped_magic - $11 (0-7). MagicGraphicsPointers holds a 3-byte pointer per spell (graphics_07B000 plus $0, $0, $800, $1000, $1000, $1800, $1800, $800), MagicPalettePointers a word per spell (palette_07D000 + $20 x n; the source bank is fixed to $0F).
lib_0118FC_part6:
HUD update and enemy gauge (file offsets 75353-75470, SNES $02:A659-$A6CE, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
UpdateHud runs once per frame at the end of the work phase (RunMainLoop step 7, RunReturnLoop, RunSubFrame) and once from ShowStatusAndSoulsScreen. It draws the enemy gauge, pays out the pending heal and EXP (lib_player_stats.DrainPendingHeal and DrainPendingExp) and redraws the parts of the HUD that hud_dirty_flags marks.
Locations $0F-$12 have no HUD: UpdateHud returns at once for location_id - $0F below 4, so the heal and EXP drains and the redraw are skipped there too, and the dirty bits are cleared (FM-A5 section 1.8 said the drains still ran; the code does not). The reduced loop of $10-$12 never calls it; location $0F still runs the full main loop (OQ-I027-2).

=== ENEMY GAUGE ===
enemy_gauge_timer ($0330) is one byte. A hit sets it to $80 (SetEnemyGauge in engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision); on the next UpdateHud $80 is the only value that draws the gauge (EnemyGaugeText: a fixed six-tile label, entry 1 of the text renderer's list TextListPointers, and the bar from enemy_gauge_hp and enemy_gauge_max). The timer then counts down by 2 per frame ($7E ... $00, 63 frames, about one second); at 0 the clear string is drawn and the timer becomes $FE; every other negative value is idle and draws nothing (OQ-I009-15).

=== HUD PARTS ===
hud_dirty_flags ($0332) is shifted out bit by bit: bit 0 HudFrameText (the backing tiles, the LEV, EXP and GEM labels and a fixed six-tile label, entry 0 of TextListPointers), bit 1 HudExpText (8 BCD digits from player_exp), bit 2 HudHpGaugeText (the HP gauge from player_hp and player_max_hp), bit 3 HudLevelText (2 digits from player_level_bcd's low byte at $1B6A), bit 4 HudGemsText (6 digits from gems_low). The menus store $1F to redraw everything; hits set bits 1 and 2, pickups bit 4.

=== NOTES ===
- The BG3 cells are written into the buffer by the text renderer (lib_text_render.PrintTextString) and reach VRAM through the upload flags it sets.
lib_012281:
Choice menu: the arrow cursor list of every question window (file offsets 74369-74506, SNES $02:A281-$A30A, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
RunChoiceMenu is called by Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts) and Cop02_PromptYesNo (no script uses it) after the option window of shared_choice_prompt_texts has been printed. A = number of options (8 bit), the high byte of A (read with XBA) = the start index (both callers pass 0), X = BG3 byte offset of the first option's arrow cell. Options are $80 bytes apart (two tile rows). The selected index is kept on the stack ($01,S) for the whole menu; menu_count ($03C4) holds the option count and menu_blink ($03C6) the blink frame counter.
The arrow is the glyph tile $2B, two tiles tall like every glyph: the lower half at X in the BG3 buffer ($7F7000) and the upper half one row above (X - $40, the buffer base $7F6FC0 + X). Only the tile byte is written, the attribute stays. Blank is tile $20.
Flow: (1) DrawChoiceCursor writes the arrow and sets vram_upload_flags bit 0. (2) WaitChoiceKeysUp calls WaitFrameReadButtons and BlinkChoiceCursor until a frame reports no new button press, so the press that opened the question cannot answer it. (3) PollChoiceKeys reads one frame at a time (joy_pressed+1: $08 Up, $04 Down, $40 Y, $80 B); any other frame runs BlinkChoiceCursor and polls again. Up on the first option and Down on the last go back to step 2 (the move is ignored). A move erases the arrow (tile $20 in both halves), plays BRK #$07, resets menu_blink, moves the cell by $80 and redraws.
Exit: B plays BRK #$18 and returns carry clear, Y plays BRK #$07 and returns carry set. In both cases the arrow stays drawn (tile $2B) on the current option, A = the index pulled off the stack and X = its arrow cell. The callers then erase the window (EraseWindowFrame at text_last_window_origin, $03F7), set vram_upload_flags = 1 and either store the index in choice_result ($03D0) or, on cancel, take the cancel pointer.

=== NOTES ===
- B = confirm and Y = cancel match the walkthrough ('Press the B Button twice to equip ... Press the Y Button to exit the menu', 01-in-the-beginning.md). The other buttons are ignored here.
- ChooseMenuRow and ChooseMenuRowAtTable (lib_0118FC_part2) are the same loop for the equipment, file-select and erase menus with their own row spacing and page swap; they share BlinkChoiceCursor with this routine.
- Nothing limits the option count except the window: the largest in use is 3.
lib_0126CF:
Staff roll (credits) scroller (file offsets 75471-75625, SNES $02:A6CF-$A768, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
ScrollStaffRollText prints a long string line by line on BG3 while scrolling the layer. The only caller is the credits actor of gv_front_end (code_007638, Y = gv_epilogue_texts.StaffRollText, 'The staff of Soul Blazer ...'); afterwards the actor waits two COP 1B delays of $F0 frames and changes scene with COP 10. The walkthrough (08-world-of-evil.md) says only 'Enjoy the credits'; the credits text is not quoted there.
Each glyph is two tiles: tile c with attribute $21 (tile bit 8 set) at the write cell and tile c with attribute $20 one row below ((X + $40) & $7FF, wrapping inside the 2 KB page). [N] ($0D) scrolls scroll_bg3_y by 32 pixels, one pixel per RunSubFrame, moves the line start four tile rows down ((old + $100) & $7FF) and clears 128 words (four rows of tile 0, attribute $20) there. [14:n] moves the write cell right by n tiles. 0 ends.
The line start lives on the stack (one word, replaced on every [N]); the routine pops it at the end, so X is not preserved.

=== NOTES ===
- Whether the clear of the new line can overwrite a line still on screen, how long the roll runs and what the 8-bit scroll does when it wraps are open (OQ-I010-17, OQ-I010-12). Spelling oddities in the credits text are OQ-I010-11.
lib_013ADA:
Default PPU layout written at boot (file offsets 80602-80678, SNES $02:BADA-$BB26, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
ApplyBootPpuLayout runs once, right after InitHardwareAndClearWram (engine_boot_main_loop BootGame). InitHardwareAndClearWram zeroes every PPU register; this routine then sets the layout that the title screen and the first scenes expect before any scene profile is applied: Mode 1 with BG3 priority, BG1 map at VRAM word $6000 (BG1SC $63, 64x64), BG2 map at $7000 (BG2SC $73), BG3 map at $5800 (BG3SC $58), BG1 and BG2 characters at word 0, BG3 characters at $4000, windows 1 on every layer with the window spanning columns 0-255, CGWSEL = $82 and the main screen TM = $07 (BG1, BG2 and BG3).

=== NOTES ===
- The values are the ones a scene profile computes later (ApplySceneProfile), so the boot layout only matters until the first scene is loaded.
lib_animation:
Record stepper used by the animation COP commands Cop92-Cop95 (file offsets 67163-67312, SNES $02:865B-$86F0, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
An actor field set drives a list of 6-byte records: $1E = animation id, $20 = step, $24 = data bank. The word list at $8000 of that bank (one word per animation id) points to the records. NextFrameRecord loads the record of the current step into the actor's work fields; CopyFrameData copies the bytes the record points to into WRAM bank $7F.
Record (6 bytes): +0 duration (0 = end of the animation), +1 word source address (bank $24,X) -> $08,X, +3 byte x 2 -> $0A,X (destination offset), +4 byte -> $0C,X (byte count - 1 for the block move), +5 byte -> $0E,X and $14,X (the wait reload). The tick counter $26,X = duration - 1.
The destination is bank $7F offset $0A,X, i.e. the CGRAM shadow $7F0000 (two bytes per colour) when the offset is a colour index x 2; a count byte of 2 (three bytes) adds $200 to the offset, which lands on coldata_buffer ($7F0200, the three COLDATA bytes). This makes the stepper a colour animation, but nothing in the code names it, so it is inferred from the destination (OQ-I026-3).

=== NOTES ===
- The block move runs through a RAM stub at $1C5C built by the scene init (lib_027912): PHB, MVN, PLB, RTS. CopyFrameData patches its two bank operands (wram_copy_stub+2): destination $7F, source = the actor's data bank.
lib_arithmetic:
Hardware multiply and divide wrappers and packed BCD (file offsets 78289-78333 and 78357-78405, SNES $02:B1D1-$B1FD and $02:B215-$B245, bank 02; the neighbours code_0131FE, code_01320E and code_013246 up to file offset 78449 are not annotated yet and are outside batch A5).

=== MODEL ===
Multiply8x8 and DivideWordByByte use the SNES multiplier ($4202/$4203) and divider ($4204-$4206): write the operands, wait the fixed time with NOPs and read the result. All three routines are entered by long call with M = 8 and X = 16 and have no side effects beyond A, B and the hardware registers. ByteToPackedBcd converts 0-255 to the packed BCD that the text control [06:n,addr] prints (digit bytes, least significant first).

=== NOTES ===
- Multiply8x8 has about 22 call sites (map streaming and sweep, scene loading, COP core, combat and spawn code, ChooseFacingAnim); DivideWordByByte only two: ChooseFacingAnim and shared_actor_helpers_bank0.
- docs/wram-memory-map.md names code_013246 as the generator of rng_state.
lib_banner_texts:
Banner strings (level up, pause banner with lair counter) and the location name list (file offsets 83222-83312 and 83906-85761, SNES $02:C516-$C570 and $02:C7C2-$CF01, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Level up: LevelUpText prints 'LEVEL UP !' (control code 03:24 = attribute) at BG3 offset $216 when the player gains a level (player_spells_level_up); LevelUpClearText overprints the same cells with ten blank glyphs.
Pause banner (lib_027572, once per frame from the main loop): when Start is pressed it pauses the music and, unless A is held, prints LocationBannerText: a 24x2 window at $186 and then the name of the current location, chosen by [TBL:&LocationNameList,1C6A]. The control code reads the WORD at $1C6A and uses it as the string number; $1C6B is never written, so the number is location_id (OQ-I011-11). When no_combat_scene is 0 it also prints LairCounterText: a 12x4 window at $51E with 'Monster Lair / Remaining' and two BCD digits of lairs_left converted to lair_count_bcd ($1B80). PauseCloseText erases both windows when the player resumes. The walkthrough confirms the lair count: 'the number of Monster Lairs in the area can be found by pressing the Start Button' (01-in-the-beginning.md).

=== LOCATION NAMES ===
LocationNameList holds 128 words (the address of the name of each location id) followed by the 128 name strings, in id order. Ids without a scene profile have a name that is a single terminator byte (25-27, 35-3B, 48-4F, 5D-63, 74-77, 7E, 7F). The ids 0F-13 have a profile but an empty name (no banner). Names are centred with a [14:n] blank run and printed with the intro font, in which the apostrophe prints as a blank and the period as '-' (so the extract shows 'Leo s Paintings' and 'St- Elles Shrine').

=== NOTES ===
- The names agree with the walkthrough and plans/doc-audit/walkthrough-crosswalk.md apart from capitalisation ('power plant', 'Shore reef of Rockbird', 'Underground lake,Lune') and the two rooms the ROM calls 'A dream 1' (ids 5A and 69, OQ-I004-14). No discrepancy row arises.
- The four Soul names (SoulOf...Text) and the menu frames lie in the same address range but belong to the menu batch (lib_menus).
lib_map_streaming:
Scroll streaming: camera update, strip building and strip upload (file offsets 65641-67162, SNES $02:8069-$865A, bank 02).

=== SCREEN MODEL ===
BG1 and BG2 each show a map that is larger than their VRAM tilemap (64 x 64 tiles = 512 x 512 pixels). A map is a grid of 16 x 16 pixel metatiles stored one byte per metatile at $7E8000 (BG1) and $7EC000 (BG2), in pages of 256 bytes (16 x 16 metatiles = 256 x 256 pixels): page = (y >> 8) x map_width_pages + (x >> 8), cell = ((y >> 4) and 15) x 16 + ((x >> 4) and 15). map_width_px ($0342, word) is map_width_pages x 256; map_height_px likewise. A metatile definition is 8 bytes (four tile words: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) at $7E2000 (BG1) and $7E2800 (BG2). Bit 9 of a tile word is not a tile bit: it is the solid flag of that quarter, the mask $FDFF removes it before the word reaches VRAM, and SetMetatileBg1 gathers the four flags into the low nibble of the tile_type_map byte ($7F8000).
The per-layer tables are word pairs indexed by X = 0 (BG1) or X = 4 (BG2): scroll_bg1_x/y and scroll_bg2_x/y, map_width_px/map_height_px, the parallax ratios ratio_x_bg1 .. ratio_y_bg2, map_base_bg1/2 ($8000, $C000), tilemap_vram_bg1/2 ($6000, $7000), tile_defs_bg1/2, tile_mask_bg1/2, tile_attr_bg1/2 and the strip buffers strip_col_bg1 .. strip_row_bg2. The scene loader fills them (lib_027912, lib_scene_asset_loader).

=== ONE FRAME ===
Work phase (NMI off): AimCameraAtPlayer stores scroll_delta_x/y; ScrollCameraByDelta adds them to scroll_bg1_x/y (clamped to the map), derives BG2 from BG1 through the ratios (UpdateLayerScrollX/Y) and sets a request bit in scroll_requests ($0396: $80 = BG1 column, $40 = BG1 row, $20 = BG2 column, $10 = BG2 row) whenever the scroll crosses a 16-pixel line (bit 4 of the position changed); BuildScrollStrips tests and clears each bit and builds the strip for it (BuildColumnStrip / BuildRowStrip), then zeroes scroll_delta_x/y. In the NMI, UploadMapStripBuffers calls UploadScrollStrips for the BG1 pair and the BG2 pair of buffers.
A strip record is 258 bytes in bank $7E: a word (the VRAM address of the strip, 0 = empty) and four blocks of 64 bytes. A column strip is one metatile column of the whole tilemap height: 2 tile columns x 64 tiles, written with VMAIN $81 (increment 32 words); a row strip is one metatile row of the whole width: 2 tile rows x 64 tiles, written with VMAIN $80. The blocks go to the VRAM address, address + 1 (or + $20), + $800 (or + $400) and + $801 (or + $420): the four 32 x 32 tile screens of a 64 x 64 tilemap. Buffer addresses: BG1 column $3000, BG1 row $3102, BG2 column $3204, BG2 row $3306.
A column strip goes at the right edge of the view (scroll x + $100) for a positive delta and at the left edge (scroll x) for a negative one; a row strip likewise below (scroll y + $100) or above. FillColumnStripBuffer / FillRowStripBuffer read 2 pages along the strip (the second is the next page, wrapping at the end of the map for columns) and CopyMetatileColumn / CopyMetatileRow expand 16 metatiles into 2 x 2 tiles each, applying the layer's tile mask and attribute.

=== ENTRY REDRAW ===
RedrawBackgroundsAtEntry (called once by the scene change code, not for location $10) places the camera on the player, derives BG2, wraps the BG2 scroll into its map and then builds and uploads 32 column strips per layer (32 x 16 px = the whole 512-pixel tilemap width), one strip at a time through UploadScrollStrips with NMI off.

=== NOTES ===
- ScaleByRatio computes scroll x numerator / divisor: the ratio word has the numerator in its low byte and the divisor in its high byte (using the PPU multiplier $211B/$211C and the hardware divider $4204/$4206), so $0201 is half speed and $0101 is the same speed.
- BuildScrollStrips is mis-decoded by the extractor (OQ-I005-7, OQ-I026-1): read its part note for the real code.
- scroll_bg1_x/y and scroll_bg2_x/y are positions in map pixels; the NMI writes them to the PPU scroll registers (WriteScrollRegisters; bg_scroll_swap exchanges the two pairs between BG1 and BG2).
lib_map_sweep_redraw:
Sweep redraw: redraws the visible map line by line from the map data (code at file offsets 69354-69929, SNES $02:8EEA-$9129; SweepStepTable 93741-94860, SNES $02:EE2D-$F28C; bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
After a map rectangle was copied (lair release, plate, NPC release scenes) the screen still shows the old tiles. The sweep step counter sweep_step ($1C75, a word) walks from 1 to 35; StepSweepRedraw is called once per frame by RunSubFrameMapSweep and, while sweep_step is non-zero, redraws one line of 16 metatiles of the 17 x 17 view (the visible map area measured from the 16-pixel aligned scroll origin sweep_origin_x/y) into vram_write_queue. The order is in SweepStepTable: columns and rows alternate outwards from the middle (column 7, row 7, column 8, row 8, column 6, row 6, ...), the last steps cover the 17th column and row because the scroll is not aligned to 16 pixels. sweep_bg1 chooses the layer: non-zero = BG1 (tilemap $6000, map $7E8000, definitions $7E2000), zero = BG2 (tilemap $7000, map $7EC000, definitions $7E2800). After step 35 the counter returns to 0 (idle).
The callers start a sweep with sweep_step = 1 and sweep_bg1 = 1 and then call RunSubFrameMapSweep 35 times; a two-layer release does a BG2 sweep first (sweep_bg1 = 0) and a BG1 sweep after it.

=== NOTES ===
- SweepStepTable: 35 steps x 32 bytes: 16 x indexes (0-$10) then 16 y indexes. Even steps are columns (x constant, y = 0-$F), odd steps rows.
lib_menus:
Field menus and screens (status and souls, talk, equipment and item menu), their HUD text and the item descriptions (code at file offsets 71932-73976, SNES $02:98FC-$A0F8, plus helpers at 74576-74639, 74730-74773 and 78198-78219; text and tables at 83313-83848 85876-86757 (ItemNameList and the item names) and 87358-90589; bank 02).

=== FIELD BUTTONS ===
DispatchFieldButtons runs once per frame from RunMainLoop with NMI on (M = 8). Order: Select or X (joy_pressed+1 bit $20; the NMI copies X into the Select bit) opens the equipment menu; B ($80) talks to the actor in front of the player; A (low byte of joy_pressed, bit 7), only when no direction is held, shows the status and souls screen. Walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: 'Press the X Button to open the menu ... Press the B Button twice to equip ... Press the Y Button to exit the menu', 'speak with him (B Button)'. The A-button screen is not in the walkthrough (OQ-I009-5). joy_pressed keeps a button as long as its release latch bit is set (engine_vblank_nmi JOYPAD note), so every chooser first waits until all buttons are up and the screens that end on a button clear the latch bits with TRB, to stop the same press acting in the field.

=== STATUS AND SOULS SCREEN ===
A BG3-only overlay (no screen blank, no graphics swap). ShowStatusAndSoulsScreen converts HP and maximum HP to BCD (hp_bcd, max_hp_bcd), clamps the strength and defence level parts (level_power, level_defense) to 12 for the display and restores them afterwards (OQ-I009-6), and prints StatusScreenText: the player name, HP / maximum, the EXP still needed for the next level (player_exp_next, 8 digits), bars for Strength and Defence (two rows each, level part over gear part) and the four equipped item names. After A is released it waits for A, B, Y or a direction, prints the souls page (SoulsScreenTitleText, then one 21-byte line per bit of souls_flags: bit 0 Magician, 1 Light, 2 Shield, 3 Detection, 4 Reality), waits for release and another press, consumes the latch and clears BG3. WaitFrameKeepClock undoes the NMI's frame_counter increment, so the frame clock stands still while the screen is open.

=== TALKING ===
RunTalkInteraction (B) disables NMI, runs FindAndTalkToActorInFront and enables NMI: the script drives its own frames. The probe point depends on the facing code (from lib_player_facing.GetPlayerFacing): code 0 (x+8, y-$10), 1 (x+8, y), 2 (x+$10, y-8), 3 (x, y-8) relative to the player's (x, y); facing 0 probes a second point two tiles up when the tile type there is 6. FindTalkableActorAt walks the actors from actor_list_tail through the $3E links and accepts the first one whose $16 has bit $0040 and whose box contains the point (x is the left edge, y the bottom edge, $10 and $12 width and height). ActivateTalkTarget needs $30,X (the script address, stored by Cop17_SetOwnParam, for example the first actor of gv_village_actors_018000) and calls it through an RTL frame: pushed bank $02 and ReturnFromTalk - 1, then the script bank (byte +$D of the actor's meta entry at $38,X) and $30,X - 1. With $16 bit $0008 the NPC first turns to face the player: TalkFacingPlayer copies the whole slot ($40 bytes) to $1A1E, ChooseFacingAnim picks the animation, the script runs, RestoreTalkedActor copies the slot back. So $16 bit $0040 = talkable and bit $0008 = turn to face the player (OQ-I005-14, OQ-I009-17).

=== INVENTORY TABLE AND SLOT BYTE ===
inventory ($1B1E) is one 64-byte table indexed by item id minus 1. The four lists of the menu are ranges of it: weapons ids $01-$08 (8 slots, $1B1E), armors $09-$10 ($1B26), magic $11-$18 ($1B2E) and items $19-$40 (40 slots, $1B36; walkthrough grid position (row, column) is slot (row - 1) x 10 + column - 1). A slot byte holds the item id in bits 0-6 (0 = not owned; an owned slot holds the id of its own slot) and bit 7 = marker: the equipped item of each list, and during a choice the cursor. DrawInventoryIcon draws a selection frame around every slot with bit 7. The equipped state is stored twice: the marker in the list and the id in the word cells equipped_weapon, equipped_armor, equipped_magic and equipped_bracelet (high bytes never written; the text codes read them as words).
Choosing from a list (ChooseFromEquipmentList, ChooseItemSlot): the cursor starts on the first slot with bit 7 set, or marks slot 0 when none is; the list is backed up to $7F0403 (only the dead cancel paths restore it); a direction moves the marker and resets menu_blink; B and Y both confirm (BRK #$18), set the marker on the slot and return A = id with carry clear. No live path cancels (CancelEquipChoice and CancelItemChoice are unreferenced, OQ-I009-14), so choosing an empty slot returns 0, which the caller stores in the equipped cell: name index 0 is the string 'not equipped'. Weapons, armors and magic are two columns of four, column-major (Right +4, Left -4, Down +1, Up -1); items are four rows of ten, row-major (Right +1, Left -1, Down +10, Up -10). A step past an end leaves the cursor where it is; stepping down from the last slot of a column goes to the top of the next.

=== EQUIPMENT MENU ===
OpenEquipmentMenu (X or Select): HDMA off (dp$42 = 0), forced blank, BG2 map at VRAM $5C00 and characters at $2000, main screen BG2 and BG3 only, colour math and windows off; saves the four scroll words (menu_saved_bg1_x .. menu_saved_bg2_y) and zeroes the live ones, saves the CGRAM buffer ($7E6000), loads the menu graphics and palette (lib_shared_012416, lib_shared_012390), runs RunEquipmentMenu. RunEquipmentMenu prints EquipMenuFrameText (tabs Weapon, Armor, Magic at $88, $98, $A8, the description window at $408 and four equipped-item lines), switches NMI and the screen on, draws the icons, uploads the BG3 page and then the BG2 icon page ($7F7800 to VRAM $5C00), and loops on ChooseMenuRow: rows 0-2 call ChooseFromEquipmentList (A = 8, Y = list base), row 3 ChooseItemSlot (A = $28, Y = $1B36). A confirmed id is stored in the equipped cell (weapon and armor then RecalcGearStats) and the frame is reprinted from its [::] marker (the window and the equipped lines only). Y on the row level leaves.
Exit: the B and Y latch bits are consumed (TRB $032B with $C0) and joy_pressed+1 is cleared; the scroll words, BG2SC, TM, CGADSUB and W12SEL are restored from the scene's shadows (tm_shadow, cgadsub_shadow, bg2sc_shadow, w12sel_shadow, stored by the scene loader), BG12NBA = 0; RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette, RestoreCgramBuffer and LoadEquippedMagicGfx put the field back in that order; when the equipped magic changed (menu_magic_on_open) all projectiles are killed and $0433 and $0434 cleared (OQ-I009-11); lib_027781_part1.ApplyPlayerWeaponPose restores the player's pose; BG3 is cleared, hud_dirty_flags = $1F, one sub-frame runs, the screen is switched on (INIDISP = $0F).

=== BG3 PAGE, ICONS ===
The BG3 text page is the 2 KB buffer at $7F7000 (bg3_tilemap_buffer), the BG2 icon page the buffer at $7F7800; vram_upload_flags bit 0 asks the NMI to send the BG3 page, bit 1 the icon page. DrawInventoryIcon writes four BG3 cells (selection frame tile $2A with its three flips, palette 3, when the slot has bit 7; else four zero cells) and the four words of the icon record IconTileRecords[id x 8] to the BG2 page (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). ClearBg3Page and ClearBg3UpperHalf fill the page with $2000 (tile 0, priority) but set their upload bit with DBR = $7F, so the TSB reaches $7F:03B8 instead of vram_upload_flags (OQ-I027-1).

=== HUD TEXT, GEAR AND DESCRIPTIONS ===
StatusScreenText, SoulsScreenTitleText, the five soul lines, EquipMenuFrameText, ItemMenuFrameText, the HUD strings (HudFrameText .. EnemyGaugeText with the repeat counts in HudRepeatCounts) and the description headers are ASCIIString parts with text control codes (the renderer is lib_text_render, batch A6: [CUR:o] cursor to BG3 byte offset o, [07:w,h] window, [03:v] attribute, [06:n,addr] n packed BCD digits, [0B:t,&c] repeat tile t by the count byte at c, [TBL:list,addr] string number (word at addr) of a pointer list, [02:n] entry n of TextListPointers (0 and 1 are fixed six-tile labels, 2 = the player name at $1B92), [04:a,b] gauge from two words, [N] newline, [::] marks the re-entry point '+M', [JMP:&s] continue at s). The extractor prints the period glyph as '-' and an apostrophe as a space ('Goat s Food').
DescriptionTextList holds 65 string pointers, index = item id (0 = empty window). Every record starts [CUR:48A][TBL:&ItemNameList,&NameIndexCells + 2 x (id - 1)] (the item name on the first line; NameIndexCells holds k + 1 for entry k because [TBL] reads its index from memory). Weapons then print the minimum swing level from WeaponMinLevelBcd (two BCD digits at $4B2) and a bar of GearStatTable strength tiles; armors only a defence bar; magic and items start the text at $50A. Stub records (ids $2B-$31, $33, $34, $3B-$3F) print their own name and [JMP] into the carrying record (DescMastersEmblemA, DescRedHotMirror, DescBrownStone) at its [::] marker. The Gem costs of magic are literal text digits (4, 8, 8, 1, 8, 20, 8, 2; OQ-I009-10).
GearStatTable has two rows of 17 bytes indexed by item id: row 0 the strength bonus of weapons ids 1-8 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12), row 1 (+$11) the defence bonus of armor ids 9-$10 (the same numbers). RecalcGearStats adds the weapon and armor entries into gear_power and gear_defense. The minimum levels (1, 5, 11, 15, 16, 19, 22, 24) are compared by the player code (player_core) with player_level_bcd; the walkthrough weapon table lists exactly these. The item names (ItemNameList and its 65 strings, file offsets 85876-86757) are noted in the ItemNameList part (batch A8).

=== NOTES ===
- StoreInventoryEntry (file offset 73977, lib_0109D6_part3, batch A4) lies between ChooseItemSlot's neighbour routines: the code of this file continues at 74040 in lib_0118FC_part2.

=== MODEL ===
RunNameEntryScreen is one blocking routine: Cop3A_EnterPlayerName calls it once, at the start of the game after the Master's first speech (walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: 'You will then get to pick a name for yourself. Choose what you will; there is no default name to be used'). The screen is plain BG3 text, drawn with PrintTextString from three strings: NameEntryFrameText (prompt, window, name line, placeholders), NameEntryGridText (the letter grid) and NameEntryCloseText (erases the window). Every change repaints both strings, which also erases the old cursor.

- X = BG3 byte offset of the cursor cell, from $03C6 (the blank cell left of 'A'); the letter is the tile at X + 2 (bg3_tilemap_buffer + 2 + X).

13 columns, two tiles (4 bytes) per column, five rows: A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, then 0-9, '-', the tile $24 (printed by the extractor as an arrow: backspace) and the tile $23 (printed as AE: accept). Rows are $80 apart (one text row is two tile rows); an extra $40 follows rows 1 and 3, so Up and Down add or subtract $C0 there and Down from row 4 / Up from row 0 wrap by $280. lib_scene_asset_loader:
Scene asset loader, Quintet LZ expander and boot hardware reset (file offsets 78281-78288 and 78450-80601, SNES $02:B1C9 and $02:B272-$BAD9, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Every scene change calls LoadSceneAssets once (lib_scene_change_init InitSceneState), after the scene-change code has put the PPU in forced blank with NMI off. So every VRAM, CGRAM-buffer and WRAM write below happens without a vblank check. dp$2F-$31 is the long pointer to the asset list (SceneAssetLists, $05:8000), set once at boot by InitHardwareAndClearWram.
The asset list has one record per scene: area, scene, commands, then a 00 byte. FindSceneRecord walks the records from the top and stops at the first whose scene equals scene_current ($0316) and whose area equals area_current ($0314). The first record is a dummy (area $53, scene $59) with no commands and the list has no end sentinel (OQ-I011-3). The other 97 records are exactly the 97 scenes that have a scene profile.
A command byte has exactly one bit set. LoadSceneAssets reads one command at a time and tries the bits from $80 down to $01 (a BIT ladder), calls the handler, which reads its own operands with ReadAssetByte, and stops on a 00 byte:
  $80 graphics   6 operand bytes  b0 start, b1 end (512-byte units, b0 bit 7 = raw), b2 VRAM page (word address b2 << 8), 3-byte pointer. LoadSceneGraphics. Skipped when asset_skip_mask bit 3 is set
  $40 palette    6 operand bytes  b0 first source colour, b1 end colour, b2 destination colour, pointer. LoadScenePalette. Skip bit 2
  $20 tileset    7 operand bytes  b0 start, b1 end (64-byte units, b0 bit 7 = raw), b2 destination offset, b3 layer mask (1 BG1, 2 BG2), pointer. LoadMetatileDefs. Skip bit 1
  $10 tilemap    4 operand bytes  type (1 BG1, 2 BG2, 0 Mode 7), pointer. LoadSceneTilemap. Skip bit 0
  $08 asset8     1 operand byte   id below $80 = scene profile, $80-$BF = jump to the label id or $40, $C0-$FF = a label. ApplySceneProfile. Never skipped
  $04 meta4      3 operand bytes  ignored. SkipMeta4Command (no record uses it)
  $02 music      5 operand bytes  b0 start command, b1 variant, pointer. LoadSceneMusic. Skip bit 5
  $01 spritemap  6 operand bytes  b0 (0 = $7E:3800, else $7E:F000), b1 and b2 ignored, pointer. LoadSceneSpritemap. Skip bit 4
Shared segments are how scenes of one world share graphics: an asset8 jump (id $80-$BF) makes FindAssetLabel scan the whole list for the matching label ($C0-$FF) and the walk continues after that label in the OTHER record, up to that record's 00. The 65 jumps in the list go to 37 labels.

=== STREAM POINTERS AND CACHE ===
Every asset pointer in a record is a 3-byte linear FILE OFFSET (lo, mid, hi). ReadAssetPointer converts it to a LoROM address in dp$29-$2B: bank = offset >> 15, address = $8000 + (offset and $7FFF). Ten 3-byte cache cells at $0407-$0424 remember the pointer of the last asset loaded into a slot: graphics by VRAM page (asset_cache_gfx0-3 for b2 $00, $10, $20, $30), tileset per layer (asset_cache_tileset1/2), tilemap per layer (asset_cache_tilemap1/2), spritemap and music. CheckAssetCache compares the new pointer with the cell, stores it and says 'load' (carry set) only when different, so entering a scene that uses the same assets in the same slots costs nothing. Palettes have no cache. A graphics b2 other than $00/$10/$20/$30 ($40 and $FF), and a tileset or tilemap type other than 1 or 2, zero the cells of that kind and always load. A zeroed cell forces a reload: other code zeroes cells to invalidate them. The cache keys on the pointer only, not on the range (b0, b1); no two commands of the shipped list share a pointer with different ranges, so that hazard does not occur.
asset_skip_mask ($03B4) is a one-shot request: an actor that warps inside a world writes $0020 before the scene change so that the music is not reloaded (15 writer sites in 13 files), and InitSceneState clears it after the load. Skipped commands still advance Y past their operands. The record walkers (FindSceneRecord, FindAssetLabel) ignore the mask.

=== QUINTET LZ ===
DecompressQuintetLz is the Quintet LZ expander of corpus/gaia-core/quintet-lz.md: a 256-byte ring pre-filled with $20, first write position $EF, a flag bit per token (1 = literal byte, 0 = back reference of an 8-bit ring position and a 4-bit length, count = length + 2), bits read MSB first with the one-hot mask dp$1E. It does NOT read the 2-byte length word that precedes every compressed stream: each caller reads it into dp$23 first. The loader decompresses to $7E:6000 (graphics and tileset staging, 8 KB at most), $7E:C000 (Mode 7 map), $7E:3800 or $7E:F000 (spritemap) and the layer map pages.

=== SCENE PROFILE, MUSIC AND VARIANT ===
ApplySceneProfile writes the PPU layout of the scene from a 12-byte record of lib_scene_profile_data (see its block note for the layout) and sets location_id, world_index, the BG tile attributes, the view height, the parallax ratios, scene_variant and no_combat_scene. scene_variant ($031E) selects which music record of the scene plays: LoadSceneMusic plays a record only when its variant byte equals scene_variant. InitSceneState clears scene_variant after the load, so it is a one-shot request: an actor may set it before the scene change; otherwise LookupSceneVariant (lib_scene_map_patches) may set it from the switch rows of SceneVariantRules; otherwise bits 7 and 6 of profile byte 11 add 1 each. The profile command is always the first command of a record, so the variant is final before the music command runs.

=== NOTES ===
- The loader never sets dp$2E, the bank byte of the copy destination [dp$2C]. Its only writer is the SPC upload (engine_spc_ipl_upload: $07 at the start, incremented per bank, $7E at the end), so the tileset and raw map copies write to the bank left by the last music upload. Whether the very first scene after boot sees $7E is open (OQ-I011-1).
- LoadMapLayer stores the height byte of a raw map with its flag bit into map_height_px (OQ-I011-2). The raw tilemap and tileset flags look unused in the shipped data.
- The LZ ring is the page $7E:0100-$01FF, which every decompression overwrites (OQ-I011-8).
- Two BRA instructions never run (after eight ASL of a non-zero byte): FindSceneRecord ends its ladder with BRA GraphicsCacheHit and FindAssetLabel with BRA loc_0139E6, a STZ BG2HOFS inside InitHardwareAndClearWram (OQ-I011-10). They pin the layout: a rebuild that keeps the bytes needs those labels at the same relative distance, so InitHardwareAndClearWram cannot move away from FindAssetLabel on its own.
- Walkthrough check: the places and bosses the walkthrough names (Grass Valley, GreenWood, St. Elles, Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Magridd's Castle, World of Evil, Deathtoll) agree with the location names that profile ids select (LocationNameList); the story text is not in the walkthrough.
lib_scene_map_patches:
Map rectangle copies of the release scenes (file offsets 69930-70388, SNES $02:912A-$92F4, bank 02), four release-scene routines that no batch has annotated yet (70389-71037), the lair state and flag map patches that run at every scene load (ApplyLairStatesToScene 71038-71152, ApplyFlagMapPatches 71153-71265, LookupSceneVariant 71266-71316, SNES $02:957E-$96D4) and FlagMapPatchTable (94861-95491, SNES $02:F28D-$F503).

=== MODEL: RELEASE SCENES ===
The rectangle is given by the copied lair record bytes in $1C6D-$1C74: release_slab ($1C6E), release_npc_x/y ($1C6F-$1C70), release_rect_x/y ($1C71-$1C72, the destination in metatiles) and release_rect_w/h ($1C73-$1C74). A slab is an alternative full-size copy of the map stored behind the live map in the $7E8000 region: slab k starts k x (map size in bytes) after the live map; its cells are copied onto the same cells of the live map (CopyMapRectFromSlab). The staging copies instead read from a rectangle of the live map itself whose position the caller put in dp$16 / $18 (record +E / +F) and write to release_rect_x/y.
CopyMapRectFromSlab keeps the high nibble of the live collision byte (the actor block bits $F0) and takes the low nibble from the slab; the staging copies replace the whole byte. A width or height of $80 or more would hang on a BCS to itself (the guard before the loops); the shipped records never do that.
Nothing is queued for VRAM by these routines: the sweep redraw (StepSweepRedraw) draws the result.

=== MODEL: SCENE LOAD ===
InitSceneState (lib_scene_change_init) calls ApplyLairStatesToScene and ApplyFlagMapPatches right after LoadSceneAssets, so the map pages and collision map they change are the ones just loaded. The two routines make the scene show what the player already did: lairs that are released stay open and gone, and rooms whose event flag is set show their opened state.
ApplyLairStatesToScene visits the 420 lair records of LairRecords (32 bytes each, $FF terminator) with a running index X over ALL records (lair_state[X] is the state byte of record X). Records of this location count in lairs_left (the number the pause banner shows). State above 0: the lair still has monsters, SpawnLairActor creates it. State 0: every monster is dead and the tile at the record's (+C, +D) becomes $FE (the lair's release switch). State below 0: the lair was released, the tile becomes $FF and the lair stops counting. The tile is written to the BG1 page $7E8000 and, when record +8 is non-zero, to the BG2 page $7EC000.
ApplyFlagMapPatches walks FlagMapPatchTable. For each row of this location whose event flag is set it copies a rectangle of the map from a hidden staging place of the same map to the visible place (CopyMapRectFromStaging): the permanent map changes of the game (opened doors and passages). LookupSceneVariant walks SceneVariantRules and is called from ApplySceneProfile (see lib_scene_asset_loader).

=== NOTES ===
- The routines from code_0112F5 to code_0114E4 (code_0112F5, code_011395 with its sub-label code_011445, code_0114D0, code_0114E4) belong to no function-map batch and stay unannotated here (OQ-I029-1).
- 13 of the 70 FlagMapPatchTable rows test event flag number $00FF (locations 00, 0E, 13, 71, 72, 73). Which flag that is and who sets it is open (OQ-I011-13).
lib_scene_profile_data:
Scene profile list and the 97 scene profile records (file offsets 92321-93740, SNES $02:E8A1-$EE2C, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
A scene profile is a 12-byte record of video and game settings that a scene's asset record selects with an asset8 command whose id is below $80 (ApplySceneProfile in lib_scene_asset_loader). The id is also the location id (location_id, $1C6A): the pause banner uses it as the string number in LocationNameList. SceneProfileList holds 128 words, one per id: the bank-$02 address of the record, 0000 for the 31 ids that have none (25-27, 35-3B, 48-4F, 5D-63, 74-77, 7E-7F). The loader subtracts the list's own address from the word and indexes from the list label with long addressing. The records are not in id order (23 and 24 come before 19, 34 before 2E).

=== RECORD LAYOUT (12 bytes) ===
  +0   TM, also TMW and tm_shadow (main screen layers)
  +1   TS, also TSW (sub screen layers)
  +2   CGWSEL
  +3   CGADSUB, also cgadsub_shadow
  +4   flags: bit 0 sets tile_attr_bg1 = $2000, bit 1 sets tile_attr_bg2 = $2000, bits 4-5 go to scene_sprite_attr+1, bit 6 view height (set 256, clear 224), bit 7 clear adds bit 8 to the BG2 tile attribute word; bits 2-3 are never read (OQ-I011-7)
  +5   BG layout: bits 0-1 screen size of the first layer, bits 2-3 of the second, bit 7 swaps the layers (bg_scroll_swap = 1): BG1SC = ($70 if swapped else $60) + size, BG2SC = ($60 if swapped else $70) + size, so the map bases are VRAM words $6000 and $7000
  +6   BGMODE ($09 = Mode 1 with BG3 priority, $0F = Mode 7 for location $10)
  +7..+10  four parallax ratios for BG1 x, BG1 y, BG2 x, BG2 y: high nibble = numerator, low nibble = divisor ($11 = same speed, $12 = half speed, $00 = fixed)
  +11  bits 0-3 world_index, bit 5 no_combat_scene, bits 6 and 7 each add 1 to scene_variant

=== WORLDS ===
world_index 0 Grass Valley (ids 00-13: the village, the Underground Castle, Leo's Paintings, the dream rooms and the intro scenes), 1 GreenWood (14-24), 2 St. Elles (28-34), 3 Mountain of Souls (3C-47), 4 Leo's Laboratory (50-5C), 5 Magridd's Castle (64-73), 6 World of Evil (78-7D). The first id of each world (00, 14, 28, 3C, 50, 64, 78: the Master's shrine rooms) has byte 4 = $E4 and byte 5 = $0F; id 11 has the same two bytes.

=== NOTES ===
- Byte 11 = $A0 or $A1-$A5 (variant + 1, no combat) occurs exactly in the 12 dream rooms (A dream: Tulip, Lisa, Bird, Stump, a dolphin, Servas, an old man, a mushroom, a cat, a soldier and the two rooms the ROM names 'A dream 1'). Byte 11 = $C0-$C5 (variant + 2) occurs exactly in six rooms: Monster in the paintings (0C), Tomb of a stone statue (22), A ghost ship (32), Poseidon (44), Tin Doll (59) and The deck of an airship (72). SceneVariantRules has a variant-0 row for the same six locations. The likely meaning is boss music until the boss switch is set, then the normal tune (OQ-I011-5, OQ-I011-6).
- Locations 0F-13 have a profile but an empty name: they are the intro and transition scenes (00/09-00/0D, and 00/0A is the Mode 7 scene), which show no banner.
- The records are read once per scene load; no code reads them again, so the list and the records can move together.
lib_shared_01230B:
Blink step of the arrow cursor, shared by the choice menu and the menu-row choosers (file offsets 74507-74537, SNES $02:A30B-$A329, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
One call per frame while a chooser waits for a key. menu_blink ($03C6) counts the calls: the low 5 bits below $18 draw the arrow (tile $2B, 24 frames), $18-$1F draw a blank (tile $20, 8 frames), so the period is 32 frames. Two short routines give the field menus and the file-select screen their own BG2 tile set and colours. That graphics_04B000 is the menu icon and frame set and MenuBgPalette its palette is a reading of the callers (OQ-I010-10).

lib_system_helpers:
HDMA channel queue and the NMI and vblank switches (file offsets 71774-71931 and 78220-78280, SNES $02:985E-$98FB and $02:B18C-$B1C8, bank 02).

=== HDMA CHANNEL QUEUE ===
HDMA channels 4-7 are handed out one per call within a frame; channels 0-2 are used by the NMI for OAM, CGRAM and VRAM transfers (HandleVBlank, engine_vblank_nmi). State lives in the direct page: dp$42 is the pending channel mask (the NMI copies it to HDMAEN), dp$44 the bit of the next free channel ($10 first), dp$46 the offset of that channel's register block from $4300 ($40 first, so channel 4 = $4340) and dp$48 is set to $6000 and never read. ResetHdmaQueue empties the queue at the start of every work phase. QueueHdmaDirect and QueueHdmaIndirect program the next channel; both are entered by long call with M = 8 and X = 16, take A.low = bank, B = PPU register index ($00-$3F, the low byte of the $21xx register) and Y = table address (load them with LDA #reg, XBA, LDA #bank, LDY #addr) and finish in the shared tail WriteHdmaChannelRegisters. HdmaDmapByRegister, indexed by the register number, supplies the DMA mode byte (one register, a register pair or the same register twice).
Indirect mode (DMAP or $40) sets both the table bank A1Bn and the indirect data bank DASBn to the bank given, so the table and the data it points to share one bank; every caller passes $7E and a WRAM table at $7800 or $7000. Direct mode reads the table as is (ROM tables binary_006A86 and binary_01B284 or WRAM).
There is no overflow guard: the fourth call shifts $80 out of dp$44 and the carry that ADC #$10 then adds (there is no CLC) makes dp$46 = $81; a fifth call per frame would write $4381-$4387, which is not a DMA channel (OQ-I009-9).

=== NMI AND VBLANK ===
nmi_enabled ($03D2) is non-zero while the frame code runs with NMI on: EnableNmi increments it, EnableDisplayAndNmi (lib_menus) increments it, DisableNmi and ForceBlankNmiOff zero it. The text renderer's input wait (lib_text_render.WaitFrameReadButtons) tests it: with NMI on it waits for the vblank, with NMI off it runs a whole sub-frame instead (RunSubFrame). WaitVBlank is the only wait for a vblank; when NMI is on, HandleVBlank runs inside it.

=== NOTES ===
- The extractor decoded ResetHdmaQueue with M = 16 (LDA #$8510 and MVP) until the M override at 71774; the real code is the 16 bytes shown now (OQ-I005-7).
- ForceBlankNmiOff, EnableNmi and DisableNmi are the NMI switches of the main loop and the scene change; their call sites are in engine_boot_main_loop, lib_menus, lib_scene_change_init and engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops.
lib_text_render:
Text renderer and dialogue renderer for the BG3 page, with their helpers and the frame and button wait helpers (file offsets 75625-78198, SNES $02:A769-$B175; list strings at 83849-83906, SNES $02:C789-$C7C1; bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
Both renderers write tile words into the BG3 tile page bg3_tilemap_buffer ($7F7000, 32 x 32 tiles, 2 bytes per tile, row stride $40); the NMI uploads the page when vram_upload_flags bit 0 is set (DmaBg3TilemapPage) and every renderer sets that bit before it returns. Offsets are byte offsets into the page; [CUR:o] gives the offset, so a text row is $40 bytes and a column is 2.
A tile word is tile (low byte) and attribute (high byte): bits 0-1 are tile bits 8-9, bits 2-4 the palette, bit 5 priority. text_attr ($03E9) starts at $20 (priority, palette 0, tile bits 0).
Two-row glyphs: the default font draws a character c as two tiles, the lower half tile c at X and the upper half tile c + $100 (attribute + 1) one row up at X - $40, so a line occupies two rows and the first line of a window starts two rows below the origin. For the first page row the upper halves land in the 64 bytes before the page ($7F6FC0-$7F6FFF, OQ-I010-7). One-row mode ([09] toggles text_attr bit 1 = tile bit 9) writes only the lower tile; the HUD strings and the name-entry placeholders use it (OQ-I010-4). [0A] toggles text_font_flip bit 7, ORed into every tile low byte, selecting tiles $80-$FF (OQ-I010-3).
Strings live in bank $02 or in the WRAM mirror below $2000 (Y < $2000 reads WRAM: the player name $1B92, the debug buffer $1F02), because the renderers read them with DBR = $02. Bytes >= $80 are dictionary words: 12-byte entries of data_dictionary (bank $10), expanded followed by one blank.

=== TWO RENDERERS ===
PrintTextString (menu renderer): prints at once, saves and restores text_attr and text_font_flip, forces DBR = $02, returns X = the last line start. 58 call sites: menus, status, HUD, gauges, title and file-select screens, name entry, Cop02 and Cop1A. No delay, no key wait, not resumable.
ShowDialogueText (dialogue renderer): typed text with a delay per glyph, key waits, paging and window scrolling, resumable. Callers: Cop01_ShowText, five sites in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return (chests and returns) and the debug scanner. It keeps the caller's DBR (bank $01 becomes $02), sets text_attr = $20, text_blip_flag = 1, text_font_flip = 0 and never restores text_attr and text_font_flip. It saves the line start in text_resume_pos at the end.

=== CONTROL CODES (operand widths as in us/stringTypes.json) ===
Code, operands, PrintTextString / ShowDialogueText:
- 00: none. End / wait for a key (WaitForButtonPress), then end.
- 01 [CUR:word]: X and the line start = word. Same in both.
- 02 [02:n] (byte): print TextListPointers[n] with PrintStringPlain / PrintDialogueString.
- 03 [03:v] (byte): text_attr = (text_attr & $E3) | v (replaces the palette bits; $24, $28, $2C = palette 1-3 with priority).
- 04 [04:a,b] (two words): the WORD ADDRESSES of the current and the maximum value (not the values); DrawGaugeBar (FM-A6 called them values).
- 05 [TBL:list,addr] (two words): list base and the WRAM address of the index; the entry is a pointer to the string.
- 06 [06:n,addr] (byte, word): n packed-BCD digits at addr, written right to left, leading zeros blanked except the last digit.
- 07 [07:w,h] (two bytes): window of w top-border tiles and h interior rows (DrawWindowFrame); the menu renderer also stores the origin in text_last_window_origin; the text cursor moves to line start + $82.
- 08 [08:origin] (word): erase the window at origin (EraseWindowFrame).
- 09: toggle one-row mode. 0A: toggle the alternate tile page.
- 0B [0B:tile,&count] (byte, word): repeat the tile 'count' times, count = the byte at the address (HudRepeatCounts). Menu renderer only; the dialogue renderer skips the three operand bytes.
- 0C [END]: ignored by the menu renderer; ends the dialogue without a key wait.
- 0D [N]: next line: line start + $40 (menu) / + $80 and scrolling at the bottom (dialogue).
- 0E [0E:n] delay n frames, 0F toggle the typing blip, 10 clear the window page and restart, 11 [FIN] blink the continue arrow, wait for B or Y, next line or restart page, 12 wait for a key: dialogue renderer only; the menu renderer prints these bytes as glyphs (OQ-I010-15).
- 13 [JMP:word]: continue the string at that address. 14 [14:n]: n blank cells (low tile bytes only; the attribute stays).
- 15-7F: glyph. 80-FF: dictionary word.

=== DIALOGUE BOX FLOW (ShowDialogueText) ===
1. First byte $10: the standard box [07:16,9] at offset $0408 (BG3 row 16, column 4; 22 x 9 interior) is drawn and the $10 is consumed. First byte $01: a plain print at the caller's X. Anything else: continue the previous dialogue at text_resume_pos (the next line when text_delay is not 0, otherwise a cleared page).
2. DispatchDialogueCode fetches bytes with ReadDialogueByte and dispatches; a glyph is written (PrintDialogueGlyph) and followed by TickAfterGlyph: it sets the upload bit, waits text_delay frames (WaitFrames, so actors keep running) and plays the blip (BRK #$07) while text_blip_flag is set; a blank does neither.
3. [N] (AdvanceDialogueLine): looks at the tile two rows below the line start. Not the bottom border (tile 4): next line, X + $80. Border: with text_delay 0 the page is prompted and restarted (PromptThenAdvance), otherwise the window interior scrolls up two rows (FindTextWindowBounds, ScrollTextWindowUp).
4. [FIN]: PromptThenAdvance measures the window, blinks the down arrow (tile $3D) under the line start (BlinkContinuePrompt: first while B or Y is still held, then until it is pressed), then goes to the next line (text_delay not 0) or restarts the page.
5. 00 (after a key wait) and [END] leave through EndDialogue: line start into text_resume_pos, upload bit set, P and DBR restored.
Window geometry written by FindTextWindowBounds: text_window_origin ($03EB, word) = interior top-left, text_window_width ($03ED) counted to tile 8, text_window_height ($03EF) counted to tile 6; the code reads the last two as words and relies on the high bytes being 0 (OQ-I010-9). Window tiles: 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 3 top, 4 bottom, 5 bottom-left, 6 bottom-right, 7 left, 8 right, $20 blank, $2B cursor, $3D continue arrow.

=== GAUGE BAR (DrawGaugeBar) ===
cur and max are read through the two addresses and only the low byte counts. The colour index is 2 * floor(cur / 10) taken before the clamp to 50 units, into data_engine_tables.GaugeColorLadder (13 words: dark blue for cur < 50, then lighter colours, white from 100); the colour goes to CGRAM colour 10 (HP bar of the HUD, bar start low byte $CC) or colour 14 (enemy bar). The bar is ceil(max / 2) tiles of $1B-$1F. This matches the walkthrough (level-up.md: 'fifty units in that bar ... each color adds ten more HP total, up to white'). A cur of 130 or more indexes past the table (OQ-I010-5).

=== WAIT HELPERS ===
WaitFrames (A frames of RunSubFrame), WaitForButtonPress (release, then press of B, Y or a direction), RunFrameReadButtons (one sub-frame, returns joy_pressed+1) and WaitFrameReadButtons (the same, or a vblank wait when NMI is on). They live in this file because the renderers use them.

=== TEXT STATE ($03E9-$03F9, $1B84) ===
text_attr $03E9 (byte); text_window_origin $03EB (word), text_window_width $03ED, text_window_height $03EF; text_resume_pos $03F3 (word; also written by the debug scanner); text_blip_flag $03F5 (bit 0, set to 1 at the start of a dialogue); text_last_window_origin $03F7 (word, origin of the last [07] drawn by the menu renderer; Cop02 and Cop1A erase it); text_font_flip $03F9 (bit 7); text_delay $1B84 (frames per printed glyph, 0 = instant; set to 3 by a new game, other values by speech scenes; the renderer reads a byte while the scenes write words, OQ-I010-1). The old reading of $1B84 as an ending flag is withdrawn.

=== DATA ===
TextListPointers ([02:n]) and its tile strings are at the end of the file.

=== NOTES ===
- Dictionary entry $06 is spelled 'Deathtole' in data_dictionary while every dialogue spells 'Deathtoll' (OQ-I010-2, DISCREPANCY with the walkthrough; unchanged here).
- The helpers WaitFrames, RunFrameReadButtons and the dialogue renderer call RunSubFrame, so they need NMI off (OQ-I005-20).
lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return:
Tile triggers under the player, the Monster Lair release and the NPC return trip (code at file offsets 68054-69353, SNES $02:89D6-$8EE9; NpcNameStrings 86758-86863 (53 words) and its strings, SNES $02:D2E6; the five chest and lair messages LairNpcNotRecalledText to ChestGemsFoundText at 90590-90723, SNES $02:E1DE-$E263; LocationAreaScene 95788, SNES $02:F62C; bank 02).

=== TILE TRIGGERS ===
CheckPlayerTileTriggers runs every frame at the start of the work phase. When the player stands on the 16-pixel grid (both coordinates have zero low nibbles) it reads the BG1 metatile at (player_x, player_y - 16): $FE (the green switch, written by SealLair) releases a lair (ReleaseLairAtSwitch, not while boss_fight_active), otherwise a pressure plate (TriggerVariantPlate) and then a chest in front of the player (TryOpenChest) are tried. The exit regions (CheckExitRegions) are tested every frame, aligned or not. Any trigger that fires zeroes the player's velocity ($04, $06). Special metatile ids: $FD intact lair, $FE green switch, $FF cleared switch, $FB closed chest, $FC open chest.
Lists: chests ChestListPointers (6-byte rows, from chest_list_ofs), exit regions ExitListPointers (11-byte rows, from exit_list_ofs), plates PlateListPointers (4-byte rows, from plate_list_ofs); every list ends with an $FF byte. The offsets are set by the scene loader.

=== LAIR RECORD (32 bytes in LairRecords) ===
Fields as used by this file (bytes 0-7 are copied to $1C6D-$1C74 for the rectangle routines): +0 location of the freed NPC's home ($FF/$80+ ends the table), +1 slab number (0-3), +2 / +3 the NPC's home tile (x, y), +4 / +5 x, y and +6 / +7 width, height of the rectangle (metatiles), +8 layer flag (0 = BG1 only, bit 0 = also BG2), +9 NPC name index (NpcNameStrings), +A state bits ORed into lair_state, +B location of the lair, +C / +D lair tile (x, y; the switch appears here), +E / +F x, y of the staging rectangle (both 0 = the lair frees an NPC; otherwise the lair opens a path), +$10-$12 lair script, +$13 monster count, +$1D warp animation, +$1E release switch word (bit index in $1ADE). The block note of data_lair_records and the part note of LairRecords describe the whole record, its counts and the six boss lairs.

=== RELEASE MODEL ===
When the last monster of a lair dies SealLair turns the lair tile into the green switch $FE. Stepping on it (ReleaseLairAtSwitch) finds the lair record, turns the switch into $FF, decrements lairs_left and then does one of two things. If +E / +F are non-zero it opens a path: lair_state = +A or $80, bit n is set in the switch array $1ADE and the released array $1A9E, and the staging rectangle is copied to the rectangle at +4 / +5 (CopyMapRectFromStaging, or ...BothLayers when bit 0 of +8 is set) while the sweep redraw (StepSweepRedraw, 35 frames per layer through RunSubFrameMapSweep) shows it. If they are zero it frees an NPC: lair_state = +A or $C0 and, when the NPC's home is the current location, the home tile gets type 1; otherwise the player is sent to the NPC's home: the return point (area, scene, x, y - 16) is saved, warp_dest is set to the home tile, area_next / scene_next come from LocationAreaScene, transition_type = $80, return_record = the lair index and return_active is incremented. In the home scene the return loop runs RunLairReleaseOnReturn every frame: when the player stands on the type 1 tile PlayLairReleaseScene prints '<name> released', steps the NPC through the slabs 0-3 and sets the arrays; otherwise it prints '<name> cannot be recalled yet!'. When the return loop ends the player is warped back (RunReturnLoop). The walkthrough agrees: freeing an NPC, opening a path or a chest by the switch beneath a lair (02-grass-valley.md lines 47, 51, 238; 03-greenwood.md line 339).
Bits of lair_state ($7F0203 + lair index): $80 = released, $40 = the NPC's return is pending (cleared by PlayLairReleaseScene and by HoldActorUntilReleased).

=== MESSAGES ===
The five strings of the chest and lair messages share one tail: ChestGemsFoundText holds the Gems line and, from its [::] marker (the '+M' entry), the key wait ([12]) and the erase of the dialogue box ([08:408]). The other four (LairNpcNotRecalledText, LairNpcReleasedText, ChestItemReceivedText, ChestEmptyText) end with [JMP:&ChestGemsFoundText+M]. text_arg ($03C8) is the one parameter: the NPC name index (lair record +9) for the two lair strings (through NpcNameStrings), the item id (through ItemNameList) for ChestItemReceivedText and the Gem amount as packed BCD ([06:3,03C8]) for ChestGemsFoundText; TryOpenChest picks the string by the content byte of the chest row (0 empty, $FF Gems, else an item id).

=== NOTES ===
- Arrays used here: $1A7E bit (chest id and $7F) = chest already opened; $1A9E bit n = lair n released; $1ADE bit n = switch n set. lib_bit_array.SetBitInArray sets bit A of the array at Y, TestBitInArray tests it (carry = set).
- The ROM text 'recieved' (ChestItemReceivedText) is kept as printed; the extractor prints an apostrophe as a space in some names (OQ-I008-14, OQ-I008-15).
- The names of NpcNameStrings are printed through the text code [TBL:&NpcNameStrings,03C8] with text_arg set to the name index.
shared_choice_prompt_texts:
Option windows of the choice menus: Yes / No, Yes, Record / Move / Quit, Record / Quit and Stay / Go back (file offsets 85762-85875, SNES $02:CF02-$CF73, bank 02).

=== MODEL ===
A string here is only the option window, never the question: the question is the COP [01] dialogue printed just before. Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts: 18 Yes / No, 6 Stay / Go back, 1 each of the other three) prints the string with PrintTextString, then calls RunChoiceMenu with the option count from its own operand, and stores the chosen index in choice_result ($03D0). Cop02_PromptYesNo (no script uses it) always prints ChoiceYesNoText.
Layout rule shared by all five strings: [CUR:o] is the window origin (BG3 byte offset, row = o / $40, column = (o mod $40) / 2; every window starts in column 4 and ends on tile row 15: origin row + h + 1 = 15), [07:w,h] draws the frame (w equals the widest option line including its leading blank, h is two tile rows per option), and every option is one text line with a leading blank (the arrow cell). Options are separated by [N][N] because a text line is two tiles tall. The trailing [CUR:c] draws nothing: c = origin + $82 (one row-pair down, one column right) is the cursor cell of the first option, and PrintTextString returns it in X, which is exactly what RunChoiceMenu expects.
The option count in the COP operand must equal the number of lines in the string: the string does not carry it.

- Which actor asks which string is documented at each part; the questions themselves are in the actor files.

'Record' is the saving; 'Move' is the later 'move on', added once the Grass Valley chief has handed over the Brown Stone (OQ-I030-1).
